highlights.title: Carrick must share burden of Man Utd's underperformance with his players
highlights.summary: "We couldn't find a way to get ourselves into the game. With the ball, without the ball, we were off it." A fair assessment from Michael Carrick, if not a wholly explanatory one.
body: Stuck in the mire of Manchester United's worst start to a league season for 40 years, the manager appeared lost for legitimate reasons. His margin for error is shrinking by the week.
Why were his side outplayed at home by the Premier League's bottom club? Why can't they hold onto leads? Why do they seem incapable of playing against 10 men?

All of these are fair questions to put to the man himself and many were asked of Carrick in the wake of Saturday's 1-1 draw with Spurs. None were answered with enough detail to satisfy, though, only really serving to hold a mirror up to what was delivered on the pitch: inadequacy.

Clearly the manager can only accept so much of the blame. His players are yet to offer a single complete performance, only bit-part displays of individualism and self-direction. Where is the cohesiveness that shaped the backend of last year? What happened to the clarity that turned a collapsed season into a third-place finish?
points: "We couldn't find a way to get ourselves into the game.
With the ball, without the ball, we were off it.
A fair assessment from Michael Carrick, if not a wholly explanatory one.

highlights.title: 26 Years Ago, 'Buffy's Worst Character Got the Replacement He Desperately Needed
highlights.summary: Xander’s status as the quintessential “comic relief” has often been tainted with a sense of “nice guy” entitlement and instances of flippant misogyny. Compared to Willow (Alyson Hannigan) or Cordelia (Charisma Carpenter), who are brilliant examples of dynamic character growth, Xander’s arc feels…
body: There is no dearth of complex, conflicted characters in Buffy the Vampire Slayer. Even our beloved Slayer, Buffy (Sarah Michelle Gellar), undergoes drastic changes while navigating adolescence and the added responsibilities of saving the world. That said, few characters come across as polarizing as Xander Harris (Nicholas Brendon), a core member of Buffy’s gang who is also an integral part of the show.

Even so, Xander’s flawed humanity is essential to ground Buffy and everyone around her. Despite never possessing any supernatural powers, Xander has demonstrated bravery in the face of abject evil and done his best to protect his friends. These admirable qualities persist in spite of his drawbacks — something that the show reminds us of in the fifth season. Titled “The Replacement,” this Buffy episode allows Xander to temporarily shed his “comic relief” role and grapple with the vulnerability of impending adulthood. This is Xander’s episode, and the character is finally nudged towards self-acceptance and growth.

highlights.title: Nuclear war and malicious use of AI threaten end of humanity by 2100, says Lancet assessment
highlights.summary: Newly established commission identifies 17 catastrophic threats to human health but says ‘realistic route to act’ on each exists. Humans could become extinct by the year 2100 due to malicious use of AI or nuclear conflict, according to a new global risk assessment.
body: They top a list of 17 major threats to human health over the next 75 years, which also includes cuts to aid spending by wealthy countries, the climate crisis and childhood malnutrition.

The experts behind The Lancet Commission on 21st Century Global Threats to Health said all the threats interact, meaning they must be addressed together – but stressed that there was “a realistic route to act” on each.

“Decisions made by leaders today will shape the health and wellbeing of the next generation,” said Prof Christopher Murray, commission co-chair and the director of the Institute for Health Metrics and Evaluation, University of Washington.

To create its list, the commission modelled how many years in good health might be lost due to sickness, disability or early deaths due to each threat, based on current trajectories – a measure known as disability-adjusted life years (Dalys).

highlights.title: Anthropic is cutting off its internal evaluations from the internet
highlights.summary: After a recent spate of high-profile incidents in which AI agents escaped containment, Anthropic is cutting off internet access for all internal evaluations. In a report Friday, the company detailed " unintended model actions," including submitting a false tip regarding an unsolved murder, that led…
body: Anthropic is is keeping its agents offline during testing until it can prevent ‘unintended model actions.’

Although the impact of these behaviors was minimal and we had already turned off live internet access for some high-risk and cybersecurity evaluations, we have now decided to expand that to include all our internal evaluations until we have confirmed that our security and monitoring measures (described in the remediation section of this post) reliably catch behaviors like these.

The ability to gain access to the live internet, even when models were supposed to be operating in isolation, has been an ongoing issue for AI companies. Many incidents, including the Hugging Face attack, involved agents that were supposed to be denied access to the internet. Yet, in case after case, the agents found creative solutions to bypass those restrictions. Physically removing internet access would certainly improve security around AI testing, but it would also limit its usefulness.

Still, you may seek out clues about whether your experience of
body: But what if there were no other audience members? (As in, deliberately… not because it was a night of badly promoted equity-waiver theater.) No friends or strangers to share immediate laughs or gasps with, let alone notes afterward? Just a small cast of actors and you, paying for the privilege of being an audience of one?

Add to this the idea that the play — about which you’re meant to know little in advance, beyond the fact that it may involve supernatural elements — takes place in a secret location, revealed only at the last minute, and even then not through anything so obvious as an actual street address. For anyone with a shy bone in their bodies, it can sound a little intimidating, knowing a band of actors is going to collectively train its sole attention on you, even before getting to the scariest aspect of all: There will be audience participation. That means you, bub.

highlights.title: AI agent makers are promising privacy — will they deliver?
highlights.summary: At this year's OpenAI DevDay, CEO Sam Altman unveiled the company's new AI agent Dots - and told the crowd that the company wants to "set a new standard for privacy in frontier AI." OpenAI would spend the day taking veiled shots at Meta's Muse, its primary competitor, for failing to keep users'…
body: Meta positioned its Muse agent as a safer alternative to OpenClaw. OpenAI promises Dots is a safer alternative to Muse.

In an age when companies hoard customers’ personal data and cyberattacks are a dime a dozen, AI labs are trying to convince users to share even more information with their agents. Their latest strategy for success is one-upping the competition by promising that unlike their rivals, they’ll keep user data away from prying eyes. The question is whether companies can keep these promises.

Nat Friedman, head of product at Meta Superintelligence Labs, wrote on X that the company’s “goal with muse was to build something like openclaw that we could make safe and secure and easy to use and scale to billions of people.” User data is stored on a secure VM, what Zuckerberg described as an “isolated linux computer with a browser, CPU, memory, and storage.” The company said that most of the effort in building Muse was related to “careful design and engineering to operate [it] more safely.” Meta’s blog post continued, “Muse can and will still make mistakes, but we expect they’ll be much less frequent and cause much less damage due to the safety systems we’ve built in.”

highlights.title: When reality TV becomes too real – and why we can’t look away
highlights.summary: In today’s newsletter, a reality TV academic – and former Bachelor contestant – speaks with us about the attachments we form with romance reality participants in the wake of a domestic violence charge against a former star.
body: Leading questions: A good friend brings her dogs when she stays with me. I kind of dread it. What can I do?

Dr Rebecca Trelease is a senior lecturer at Auckland University of Technology’s school of communication studies in New Zealand, and during the first year of her PhD, she was also a participant on The Bachelor New Zealand. She’s been a “massive fan” of reality television since the early Big Brother days, and believes many fans engage with popular culture in a critical, scholarly way – regardless of their formal qualifications. But of her time on camera, and the media coverage surrounding it, she says: “It was really fascinating to see it first-hand, but it was also really awful at times and I wouldn’t recommend it.”

Alyx: Tell me a bit about the media cycle surrounding romance reality shows, and the connections that viewers are encouraged to develop with the cast? Rebecca: In romance reality, in some shows we want to see a main hero looking for love across the season, while in others, we want to see two individuals come together and follow them from meeting at the altar, to “are they gonna stay together at the end?”.

body: This trailer focuses on the show's central mystery: what happened to 38 replicants who went missing over the past year? That mystery causes the paths of Cora, who's a fugitive on the run, and Olwen, a Replicant who's near death, to cross. Eventually, they'll uncover a whole conspiracy connected to a criminal gang of replicants who don't think replicants should feel the need to act human.

Speaking to Polygon in September, showrunner Silka Luisa teased that Blade Runner 2099 is " Chinatown set in the world of Blade Runner. It's really about Cora and Olwin investigating missing people, just like they do in the films." Like its predecessors, this new trailer shows that Blade Runner 2099 is shaping up to be a thoughtful sci-fi mystery thriller dealing with existential ideas about AI, humanity, and intimacy.

Prime Video also released a new poster for the series, sporting the tagline, "Welcome to a future we no longer control." That alludes to the fact that, by 2099, Los Angeles is now dominated by Replicants rather than humans, which we also get a more in-depth look at in this new trailer.
All eight episodes of Blade Runner 2099 will be released on Prime Video on the same day: Nov. 25.

body: Chinese director Gu You's conclusion to his 'Landscape' trilogy too often steps into maudlin territory, but rights itself whenever it focuses on everyday details in its portrait of three generations of grieving women.

Somewhat heavily expository dialogue informs us that Yue, formerly a fashion director in Beijing, has recently returned with Moon to the family apartment in the city of Hangzhou in southeast China. Home to Luna and her late husband for decades, it’s a roomy, rambling space with spectacular views of the Qiantang River and, in Zhou Xingyu’s excellent production design, a storied buildup of clutter. Mikiya Takimoto’s camera lingers affectionately on stacked bookshelves — not even old cassette tapes have been thrown away — and desktops heavy with ornaments, notes and photographs that reveal in shorthand a life rich in love. Even in death, the man maintains a palpable presence in the home.

highlights.title: Still wielding a chainsaw at 85: the Australians restoring nature in retirement
highlights.summary: For a growing band of older Australians, retirement has become an unlikely second act, spent rewilding mountains, counting sea slugs and coaxing damaged country back to life. Get our weekend culture and lifestyle email.
body: When Susan Downes stepped into the hallway of an old farmhouse for sale in York, Western Australia, she felt an oddly certain sense of knowing. “Oh, this is my house,” the retired GP remembers thinking. There was just one problem: it came with 200 hectares.

Widowed and with her children grown, Downes, then in her 60s, was finally able to act on a long-held wish to move to the countryside. She had imagined something modest: an old house with “a little bit of garden and stuff”. Two hundred hectares was rather more than she had in mind, no matter how charming she found the high ceilings. “I thought, the house is lovely, but I can’t possibly do that.”

But the property had gotten under her skin. Returning for another look two weeks later, she discovered Mount Mackie, a 295-metre hill at the back of the farm where ancient York gums and wandoos had survived about 150 years of grazing. Almost all of the understorey had disappeared. “These magnificent old trees” were all that remained. “I felt a great connection to the land,” she says.
points: For a growing band of older Australians, retirement has become an unlikely second act, spent rewilding mountains, counting sea slugs and coaxing damaged country back to life.

highlights.title: DistroKid has been quietly taking down songs in response to UMG lawsuit
highlights.summary: Artists are taking to social media to complain that DistroKid has unceremoniously removed their work without notice. Now DistroKid has confirmed to The Verge that the takedowns are a direct response to claims made by UMG.
body: Artists are frustrated with the lack of transparency around DistroKid removing their songs.

Musician and self-described “Video Game boy” McGwire reported that six of his songs had been removed from streaming. As has been the case with others, McGwire says that there was no communication from DistroKid before or after the removals, and that he had to contact the company for an explanation.

DistroKid also makes it exceedingly difficult to contact them. McGwire first had to have a “lengthy circular conversation” with a bot before getting hold of a live agent. One of the songs removed was a cover of Stevie Wonder’s “Isn’t She Lovely,” which he claims to have had a proper license for. Another track used a beat he purchased through a marketplace, which others had also licensed.
Most infuriating for McGwire was a song removed for an uncleared sample. The song he allegedly sampled was released two years after his track.

highlights.title: 2024's Most Inventive Slasher Movie Officially Sets Sequel Release Date
highlights.summary: Horror fans are currently in the midst of Spooky Season, but there are plenty of slasher scares still on tap for the winter. That includes the highly anticipated sequel to 2024's In A Violent Nature, the inventive microbudget slasher movie that puts a twist on the supernatural serial killer formula.
body: On Saturday, at New York Comic Con, horror streaming service Shudder announced the release date of In A Violent Nature: Part 2, which will continue the story of urban legend Johnny's killing spree.
Shudder and Independent Film Company officially revealed at NYCC that In A Violent Nature: Part 2 will arrive exclusively in theaters on Feb. 12, 2027.
Ry Barrett, who returns as the masked killer Johnny, announced the date on Saturday. The announcement came shortly after In A Violent Nature: Part 2 ’s world premiere at Fantastic Fest in September.

According to an official synopsis, In A Violent Nature: Part 2 picks up immediately after the events of the first film, with new victims for Johnny to dispatch and a deeper dive into the killer's lore. "Johnny’s violent rampage leads him to a summer camp just as a young, outcast camper is forced to spend the night with his counselor sister and her friends at their annual end-of-season party," the film's description reads. IFC and Shudder promise the film is "pushing the possibilities of extreme kills even further" with "uncompromising gore and unforgettable kills." Johnny's signature murder weapon is a rusty metal hook attached to a large chain.

highlights.title: Philippines Revamps International Co-Production Fund With Minority and Majority Tracks, Unveiled at Busan Market
highlights.summary: The Philippines has revamped its International Co-Production Fund (ICOF) around two tracks, with the amount of cash on offer tied to the size of the Filipino stake in a project.
body: The Film Philippines Office (FPO) unveiled the new framework at the Busan International Film Festival ‘s Asian Contents & Film Market.

The Minority Track is for international productions in which a Filipino producer is the junior partner. Features and series can draw up to PHP7 million ($113,000), with documentaries and shorts capped at PHP3 million ($48,000).

The bar is lower here. Filipino producers need a stake of 10% or more, and the production must hire either two Filipino above-the-line talents or three Filipino crew members in key creative or technical roles. Applicants must also show how the film will reach audiences outside the Philippines.

Both tracks offer the same top-ups. Qualifying ASEAN co-productions earn an extra PHP1 million ($16,000), and projects that clear a cultural test can collect up to PHP2 million ($32,000) more. The FPO noted that the dollar figures may vary with exchange rates.

highlights.title: How to enable Live Activities on iPhone and CarPlay
highlights.summary: Live Activities put the most important real-time information from apps in a place where it's easy to keep an eye on.
body: Keep track of important updates without having to open the app every two minutes.

At a time when most Android phones had already switched to tiny hole-punch cutouts to house their front-facing cameras, the iPhone 14 Pro launched with a long pill-shaped cutout. Apple has used this as its standard since then, aside from the budget "e" phones and iPhone Duo, and even made it smaller for the iPhone 18 Pro series.

This is because iPhones pack more than just a camera inside the cutout; there are additional sensors required for Face ID to work. Instead of hiding the pill with cleverly designed wallpapers, Apple leaned into it with the Dynamic Island, using the surrounding area to turn an otherwise awkward design constraint into a useful part of the iOS experience.

Your iPhone's Live Activities show up on the Dynamic Island when using your phone. They display information you might want to keep an eye on without having to constantly switch back to the associated app: timers, navigation directions, music playback and sports scores can be displayed as Live Activities. Many third-party apps like food delivery and flight tracking services have also adapted to use the Dynamic Island.
points: Live Activities put the most important real-time information from apps in a place where it's easy to keep an eye on.

highlights.title: Real Madrid’s Vinícius Júnior sent off for hair-pulling in victory over Villarreal
highlights.summary: Yan Diomandé earned Real Madrid a tight 1-0 victory over Villarreal to keep them six points behind La Liga leaders Barcelona, even though winger Vinícius Júnior was sent off for hair pulling.
body: Vinícius, on as a substitute, scored but his goal was disallowed and then he was dismissed after a VAR review showed he had pulled the hair of Villarreal’s Nathan Saliba.

José Mourinho’s side battled through the final stages with 10 men, holding on to win and provisionally going third. But the red card left a bitter taste for Real, with Vinícius running the risk of a potential ban which could keep him out of El Clásico on 25 October.
“I don’t know what’s going on with the referees, with this red card, I don’t understand,” said the Madrid midfielder Aurélien Tchouaméni. “But the most important thing is the victory.”

Kylian Mbappé was fit to start the match for Madrid after suffering a knee problem playing for France during the international break. There were a smattering of whistles for the superstar forward, with some fans believing he has been unprofessional in recent weeks, but also applause from others.

highlights.title: Forget John Wick, the Ultimate Action Thriller of the Century Is Officially Streaming on Netflix
highlights.summary: Some of my favorite movies are about ordinary dudes who turn out to be a nightmare for anyone dumb enough to cross them. Pierre Morel’s Taken twisted Liam Neeson into the patron saint of revenge. Then came John Wick with an angry Keanu Reeves to perfect that very specific formula.
body: But Denzel Washington just hits different. Having starred in the 2004 masterwork of action, Man on Fire, Washington knows perfectly well how to captivate as a tired ex-soldier pushed to the brink. While it might not have the same Tony Scott flair, 2014’s The Equalizer still carries that satisfying dad-action energy — but in this film, Washington’s kills feel even more visceral at times. It may not be the pinnacle of the genre, but it’s still one of my dad’s favorites, and it just dropped on Netflix, making now the perfect time to revisit one of Washington’s best characters.

Directed by Antoine Fuqua, who previously teamed up with Washington for Training Day, The Equalizer takes inspiration from the 1980s television series of the same name. Unlike the show's private detective, who uses his particular set of skills to help people who have nowhere else to turn, Washington instead steps into the role of Robert McCall, a quiet Boston hardware store employee who spends his nights reading books at a local diner. When a teenage diner regular (Chloë Grace Moretz) runs into serious trouble with the Russian mob, McCall is forced to fold back into the person he long abandoned to protect her.

highlights.title: Venta review: a humidifier that fixes the worst part of humidifiers
highlights.summary: Venta’s evaporative mechanism add cool moisture without mist, mineral dust or disposable filters. Sign up for the Filter US newsletter, your weekly guide to buying fewer, better things.
body: I f you live with forced-air heating, you know that winter can bring chapped lips, dry eyes and waking up with a scratchy throat. A common ultrasonic humidifier attacks the issue with an eye-catching stream of cool mist – and they work well. But as I found out after setting up two of them, they also bring an unwelcome guest: dust.

Minerals dissolved in the water travel with those droplets, leaving a messy residue behind. With two running, it was like an invisible dust storm rolled through every day, raining fine white powder everywhere. It coated furniture, clogged air filters and even choked computer fans. I don’t mind dealing with household dust, but a maddening amount accumulated daily.

Distilled water can fix this issue, but it would also saddle me with the plastic waste, hassle and expense of hauling gallons of water home from the store every week. Instead, I started looking for a different approach and found Venta humidifiers, which use natural evaporation to efficiently humidify air while leaving the minerals behind.
points: Venta’s evaporative mechanism add cool moisture without mist, mineral dust or disposable filters.
